causes.text: Chinese property developer Evergrande teetered on the brink of default, missing bond payments and sparking fears of contagion across global markets.

source_info.title: World shares tumble as China Evergrande contagion fears rise

effects.text: Bank of America's shares fell about 3% as Evergrande's potential default triggered global risk-off sentiment and raised concerns about banks' exposure to Chinese real estate.

source_info.title: World shares tumble as China Evergrande contagion fears rise

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Evergrande missed bond payments and edged toward default, raising alarm about China's property sector solvency.
Investors feared that Evergrande's liquidity crisis could spill over into global financial markets, triggering broader risk aversion.
Bank of America's stock declined by roughly −3% amid a global sell-off of financial shares driven by contagion fears.

rationale: Evergrande's near-default highlighted systemic fragility in China's real estate sector, and the resulting risk-off sentiment weighed heavily on global bank stocks, including Bank of America-even absent direct exposure.
counterfactual_analysis: If Evergrande had met its debt obligations or disclosed a credible rescue plan, global sentiment may have remained calmer and Bank of America's shares might not have dropped.

adversarial_confounders.text: Simultaneous concerns over U.S. debt ceiling negotiations or Fed taper signals may also have influenced sentiment.
adversarial_confounders.impact: These factors contributed to risk aversion, but the Evergrande incident was the most immediate catalyst in global markets.

details.pestel_factor: Political - U.S. export controls on advanced chips to China
details.commentary: Tighter U.S. rules on shipping high-end GPUs to China reduced Nvidia's access to a key growth market for AI hardware. The risk of further restrictions or customer workarounds made investors question how sustainable Nvidia's prior growth trajectory would be.

Export controls initially sparked fears of a sharp revenue hit, prompting a sell-off in Nvidia and related names. As the company developed adjusted products and demand proved resilient elsewhere, better-than-feared results partially offset those worries, creating a balancing loop.
